steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The UK produces approximately 9.5 million tonnes of food waste per year; about 70% of this was intended for human consumption and could have been eaten. | Key Fact: Food waste occurs at every stage: production (crops left in fields), processing (trimming, quality rejection), retail (overstocking, past display dates), and consumer (over-buying, cooking too much, not using leftovers). | Key Fact: Households produce the most food waste (around 70% of the UK total), mainly from buying too much, not using food before it spoils, and cooking larger portions than needed. | Key Fact: When food waste goes to landfill, it decomposes anaerobically, producing methane — a greenhouse gas 25 times more potent than carbon dioxide.
